title: API-13's disk-identifier row sets no length cap, though SEC-29 caps individual fields per API-13 (SEC-29, API-13)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22.

**The problem.** `SEC-29` says "Request bodies MUST be size-capped globally, and individual fields MUST be capped per `API-13`." `pv-6p8` added an `API-13` row for disk identifiers, `target.identifier` and `layout.drives[].identifier`: "a JSON string, non-empty after normalization (`RSC-46`)". It sets no length cap. The panel's reviewed form set none either.

Every other caller string in `API-13`'s table has one: hostname "1–253 characters", offer identifier "1–256 characters", catalog image "1–256 characters". So a single disk identifier can fill the global body cap ("2 MiB is a reasonable default"). It is then stored in the operation's request and compared in the worker.

**Example.** A caller sends a 1.9 MiB `target.identifier`. Engine A refuses it, reading `SEC-29` as requiring a per-field cap. Engine B admits it, because `API-13` states none, and repeats the comparison in the worker (`OPS-23`). Both conform to `API-13` as written.

**Question.** What is the disk identifier's length cap in `API-13`, if any? Should `SEC-29` say that a row without a cap is capped only by the body cap?

title: CNF-200's "rejected" doesn't say whether a path-shaped disk identifier is refused at admission or aborts integrity (CNF-200, API-13, RSC-26, CNF-363)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22.

**The problem.** `CNF-200` says "A rootfs install naming a drive by unstable device path is rejected; the layout carries stable identifiers checked against the inventory fingerprint, exactly as raw-disk does." It does not say how a path-shaped `layout.drives[].identifier` is rejected.

- After `pv-6p8`, `API-13`'s new row admits any "JSON string, non-empty after normalization (`RSC-46`)". `/dev/sda` is such a string, so it is not refused `invalid_request` before enqueue.
- It then resolves against the re-read inventory under `RSC-26`, which says "An identifier that does not resolve to exactly one device MUST abort `integrity` before any write". The install is admitted, enters rescue, and aborts `integrity`.
- `CNF-363` case (14) avoided the clash by using an unmatched identifier "that is not path-shaped".

**Example.** Engine A refuses `{"identifier": "/dev/sda"}` with `invalid_request` before enqueue, reading `CNF-200`'s "rejected" as an admission refusal. Engine B admits it, boots rescue, and aborts `integrity`. Both can claim to pass `CNF-200`. Under `API-13` as amended, A refuses a value the admission table admits. B reboots the customer's machine into rescue for a request no real disk can match.

**Question.** Does a path-shaped disk identifier fail at admission (a new `API-13` rule) or at resolution (`integrity`, as `RSC-26` reads now)? `CNF-200` then asserts that outcome, not "rejected". If the answer is resolution, does `CNF-363` case (14) drop "that is not path-shaped", so that it also drives the stale-path echo? The review of `pv-6p8` noticed that the form's case says only "A well-formed identifier that matches nothing aborts `integrity`".

title: RSC-46's "ASCII whitespace" is undefined, and common definitions disagree on U+000B (RSC-46, CNF-363)
description:
Found during the `pv-6p8` drain review (branch `pv-6p8`), 2026-10-22. This is the reviewed form's out-of-scope bullet about pinning "ASCII whitespace" to U+0009–U+000D plus U+0020. Two readers proposed it in r61c.

**The problem.** `RSC-46` normalizes an identifier with "trim ASCII whitespace, ASCII-lowercase, then strip exactly one leading `0x`", and the wire values are "trimmed of ASCII whitespace". The set doesn't define "ASCII whitespace", and common definitions disagree on U+000B (vertical tab):
- WHATWG Infra's "ASCII whitespace" is U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D and U+0020. It excludes U+000B.
- C `isspace` and Python `bytes.strip()` include U+000B.

The trimmed value is what the wire shows, what matching compares, and what the `inventory_fingerprint` hashes.

**Example.** A disk's serial is read as `"ABC123\v"`. Engine A trims it to `ABC123`. Engine B keeps `ABC123\v`. They show different `serial` and `identifier` values and compute different fingerprints over the same disks. `CNF-363` case (2) asserts the fingerprint "equals an independently computed hash". Its outcome then depends on which definition the conformance suite uses.

**Question.** Pin "ASCII whitespace" in `RSC-46`, for example to U+0009–U+000D plus U+0020, or cite a definition?
